title: Balance assertions distinguish tolerance from exact Money equality
question: A balance tolerance policy is not approximate comparison for FinKore Money.

evidence.title: Balance assertions use a separate decimal tolerance policy
explanation: An explicit balance tolerance takes precedence. Otherwise the source derives tolerance from the asserted Decimal exponent and a configured multiplier. It compares the accumulated currency-specific balance to the expected amount and reports errors only when absolute difference exceeds that tolerance.
A ledger balance-assertion policy, outside current Core ledger/reconciliation scope. Its decimal tolerance does not redefine exact Money equality or authorize approximate monetary conformance checks.

evidence.title: Probability admission is type-based slack without renormalization
explanation: Initial distributions and transition rows reject negative mass and accept a total deviation up to the sum of eight floating eps units per entry; accepted rows are not rescaled. fold_row applies nonzero-edge callbacks before checking final row total.
Probability tolerance is not Money equality. Invalid final sums can leave injected callback effects, though project-owned buffers do not escape as a returned valid projection. No runtime execution.
